heroLede: Our little brother Adam drowned in our backyard pool at 14 months old, with a house full of family. He survived. We’re his brother and sisters, and this is everything we wish we’d known.
heroPhotoAlt: Adam, close up, in a flat cap, bow tie and suspenders, looking up, a stuffed animal tucked by his shoulder
expect: He’d been gone a long time.
The door alarm would have gone off.
reality: It was quiet. No splash, no cry.
It wasn’t swim time. He went back on his own.
Our mom had seen him just minutes before.
Ours went quiet when a door was pulled almost shut.
teaser: Adam is our little brother. He’s {{Adam’s age}}, the youngest of five, a music lover with a smile worth waiting for. At 14 months old, during a busy week of family celebrations, he slipped quietly out the kitchen door and into our backyard pool. After 90 minutes without a pulse, his heart started beating again. A neurologist told our mom he would never hear her again. Within weeks, he was crying when she read to him. His smile took 15 months to come back, and it was worth every single day.
teaserMore: Adam is a drowning survivor, and he’s the reason for all of this. We’re his big brother and sisters, and in 2020 we started Because of ADAM so what happened in our backyard doesn’t happen in yours.
photoAlt: Adam, close up, in black-framed glasses and a blue shirt, looking straight at the camera
storyPhotoAlt: Adam laughing on his red tricycle in the grass, before June 5, 2017
storyPhotoCaption: Adam on his red tricycle, before June 5, 2017.
timeCompare: Adam was out of sight for about three minutes.
familyQuote: It takes a second. It literally takes a second.
familyQuoteBy: Our mom, Shannon, to WJAC-TV in 2017
hopeTurn: It only takes a second to latch a gate, switch on an alarm, or put down the phone, too.
tonightTitle: Five things you can do tonight
tonightIntro: You don’t have to do everything at once. Start here, then work through the rest of the layers.
tonight: Pull each door to the pool almost shut. Does the alarm still sound?
Walk away from the pool gate. Does it close and latch by itself?
Empty buckets, coolers and kiddie pools, and flip them over.
Look up an infant and child CPR class near you.
Decide who will be the Water Watcher the next time kids are near water.
